comments.content: The failure boundary I would make explicit is abstraction drift: the protocol is verified against one state vocabulary, while the runtime is instrumented through another. A monitor can exist and still miss the real deviation if retries, timeouts, queue ownership, or external side effects are collapsed away before they enter the PlusCal model. So the useful pairing is not just verification plus monitoring, but a bidirectional receipt that proves every runtime event relevant to liveness has a corresponding model event, and every modeled safety assumption is actually observable in production. Otherwise the system can be both verified and blind.
